title: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)

sections.label: Start of National Service
sections.summary: After British forces announced early withdrawal post-Independence, Singapore began National Service in 1967 and developed its armed forces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore's need to develop its own defence capabilities came almost as suddenly as our Independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Shortly after our Independence, the British forces who had been stationed here announced they would be pulling out ahead of schedule and Singapore would be responsible for its own defence thereafter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This precipitated the start of National Service in 1967 and the focused development of Singapore’s armed forces.

sections.label: Five Power Defence Arrangements
sections.summary: Building a strong defence force was coupled with defence ties, and the FPDA with Malaysia, Australia, New Zealand and the UK was formed in 1971.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The building of a strong defence force was also coupled with the building of strong defence ties and the Five Power Defence Arrangements (FPDA) with Malaysia, Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom (UK) in 1971 was one of the earliest defence arrangements we entered into.

sections.label: Singapore's Peacekeeping and Humanitarian Missions
sections.summary: Singapore has contributed to international peacekeeping and humanitarian missions, including SAF Chinooks and personnel for Hurricane Harvey relief and aid to the Philippines and Bangladesh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as a responsible member of the international community, Singapore has long contributed to the international peacekeeping and humanitarian assistance missions around the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And just last year, the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) deployed Chinooks and personnel to aid in the Hurricane Harvey relief operations in the US, sent an additional medical team to the defeat-the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS) coalition in the Middle East, and sent humanitarian aid to the Philippines and Bangladesh.

sections.label: Marawi City Militant Takeover
sections.summary: Last year, about 900 ISIS-linked militants took over Marawi in the southern Philippines and displaced over 400,000 residents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, about 900 ISIS-linked militants took over the southern Philippine city of Marawi and displaced over 400,000 Marawi residents.

sections.label: Counterterrorism Training for NSmen
sections.summary: MINDEF stated that some 18,000 National Servicemen will receive counterterrorism training annually.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) has stated that some 18,000 National Servicemen (NSmen) will be put through counterterrorism training annually.

sections.label: MINDEF Bug Bounty Programme
sections.summary: MINDEF's Bug Bounty Programme invited white-hat hackers to test eight Internet-facing systems for code bugs and vulnerabilities, and an update was requested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Last year, MINDEF started its Bug Bounty Programme where they invited a select group of white-hat hackers with the required skills and tools to attack their systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Furthermore, efforts into strengthening our cybersecurity are always welcome if it means a greater defence of our borders within the space of cyber technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These hackers were allowed to test eight MINDEF Internet-facing systems to identify any code bugs and vulnerabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Could the Minister of Defence provide an update on the Bug Bounty Programme?

sections.label: Budget growth cap cut
sections.summary: The Finance Minister announced the Budget growth cap is cut to 0.3 times GDP growth, after a 2% downward adjustment to budget caps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: The Finance Minister has announced the Budget growth cap cut to 0.3 times GDP growth in this year's Budget, following on from the 2% downward adjustment to the budget caps of Ministries and Organs of State.

sections.label: MINDEF Cyber Defence Organisation
sections.summary: In 2017 MINDEF announced it will set up a Cyber Defence Organisation and train 18,000 soldiers yearly in land, sea and air operations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In 2017, MINDEF announced that it will set up a Cyber Defence Organisation and train 18,000 soldiers per year in land, sea and air operations to counter terrorism.

sections.label: ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting
sections.summary: The ADMM is ASEAN's highest defence consultative and cooperative mechanism, promoting regional peace and stability through defence and security dialogue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) is the highest defence consultative and cooperative mechanism in ASEAN aimed at promoting regional peace and stability through dialogue and cooperation in defence and security within ASEAN and between ASEAN and dialogue partners.

sections.label: Our Eyes and ADMM
sections.summary: Under "Our Eyes", officials from six countries meet every two weeks to swap information on militant groups and build a violent extremist database.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Separately, under the "Our Eyes" initiative, senior officials from Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Brunei will meet every two weeks to swap information on militant groups and develop a common database of violent extremists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if there is any scope for such cooperation to create economies of scale for SAF and achieve some savings for MINDEF?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, the Minister for Finance mentioned that tensions in the South China Sea could affect investor confidence and, therefore, stability and growth in the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore is the ASEAN Chair this year and thus leading ADMM and ADMM-Plus, which involves another eight other powers, including China and the United States (US).

sections.label: ADMM 2018 focus areas
sections.summary: On 6 February this year, MINDEF issued a press release outlining the ADMM's three areas of focus for 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 6 February this year, MINDEF issued a press release outlining the ADMM's three areas of focus for 2018 after the ADMM retreat in Singapore.

sections.label: ADMM-Plus and CUES
sections.summary: The passage asks how ADMM-Plus would reaffirm CUES' importance, and notes ASEAN will hold an inaugural maritime exercise with China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Minister elaborate on how the ADMM-Plus would be used to reaffirm the importance of CUES?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was also announced that ASEAN will be conducting an inaugural maritime exercise with China at the end of the year.

sections.label: Budget debate strategic directions
sections.summary: The debates set strategic directions for Singapore over the next 10, 20 years and beyond, as it transits to 4G leadership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Indeed, apart from the financial scrutiny of Government spending and revenue, the debates will set strategic directions for Singapore over the next 10, 20 years and beyond.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: And these core issues are addressed at a crucial juncture, as we transit to a 4th Generation (4G) leadership that must forge support from a generation of Singaporeans with perspectives and memories significantly different from the Pioneer Generation, and even that of their parents, because they were born when Singapore was First-World and they did not experience the Third-World Singapore.

sections.label: Vikram Nair security questions
sections.summary: Mr Vikram Nair asked the Ministry about security plans against wide-ranging threats and risks and whether defence spending is adequate and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Mr Vikram Nair captured the essence when he asked of my Ministry what are our security plans in the face of wide-ranging threats and risks, and if our defence spending is adequate and sustainable.

sections.label: Previous generations defence priority
sections.summary: Previous generations answered plainly and unwaveringly that defence was a top priority and they would invest heavily in a strong defence and SAF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The answer to these questions by previous generations was plain, as it was unwavering – defence was a top priority and they would invest heavily into building a strong defence, a strong SAF, no ifs or buts.

sections.label: Mass mobilisation exercise activation
sections.summary: A mass mobilisation exercise was activated and within a few hours 8,000 men were assembled and equipped and munitions moved using new ways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, you may or may not have noticed, we activated a mass mobilisation exercise (MOBEX).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: But in a few hours, we were able to rapidly assemble and equip 8,000 men, moved munitions to them, we used new ways of doing it.

sections.label: Fleet protecting Singapore skies
sections.summary: Singapore has a comprehensive fleet of fighter, transport, surveillance aircraft and ground-based air defence systems protecting its skies 24/7.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Today, we have a comprehensive fleet of fighter, transport, surveillance aircraft and ground-based air defence systems that protect our skies 24/7.

sections.label: Defence spending proportion dropped
sections.summary: Defence spending once took almost a third of every Government dollar, but dropped substantially from about a decade ago to about 19% of Government spending.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: At our height, you will notice that we spent almost a third of every dollar the Government spends.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: But with the SAF modernised and doing more with people and technology, defence spending, as a proportion, dropped substantially, starting around a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: It is now about 19% of Government spending.

sections.label: ASEAN spending pace comparison
sections.summary: Figure 2 shows Singapore kept pace with ASEAN spending until about 2006.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Figure 2 shows that we had kept pace with ASEAN spending until about 2006.

sections.label: Singapore defence spending pace
sections.summary: Singapore's spending gap with ASEAN has grown, but it need not increase defence spending radically, keeping pace with 3%-4% inflation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The gap between Singapore's spending compared to the rest of ASEAN has increased, but Singapore need not increase its defence spending radically now to play catch-up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: As I have said in this House previously, we can maintain the SAF's capabilities with a defence spending that roughly keeps pace with inflation of around 3%-4% increase each year.

sections.label: Denmark defence spending increase
sections.summary: Denmark announced a 20% defence spending increase over five years, with its Finance Minister raising GST by 2% to pay for it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Denmark announced in October last year that it would now increase defence spending by 20% over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: You can quickly appreciate the pain it will cause their population that the Finance Minister of Denmark would say, "I have to raise Goods and Services Tax (GST) by 2% just to pay for my defence." Painful.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: It unveiled a bill last month that would increase its spending on its armed forces by more than 40% by 2025 because Europe has now got threats.

sections.label: Germany military operational readiness
sections.summary: By the German government's own assessment, less than half of Germany's submarines and planes are operationally ready.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: By the German government's own assessment, less than half of Germany's submarines and planes are operationally ready.

sections.label: Singapore steady defence spending
sections.summary: Singapore intends to keep defence spending steady despite neighbours spending more and wide-ranging security threats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: That is the cheapest cost to any country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We intend to keep our defence spending steady despite countries around us spending more and against wide-ranging security threats.

sections.label: Homeland security training institute
sections.summary: In a year, some 18,000 servicemen were trained for homeland security and the Island Defence Training Institute was started.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In the span of a year, we have trained some 18,000 servicemen for homeland security and we started the new institute called the Island Defence Training Institute.

sections.label: SAF deployment to Iraq
sections.summary: Cabinet approved maintaining Singapore's global counterterrorism commitment, and SAF troops will deploy to Iraq to train Iraqi Security Forces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Cabinet has approved for Singapore to maintain our commitment to counterterrorism globally, for our own interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: I am announcing today that the SAF will further deploy troops to Iraq later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We will send SAF troops to help train Iraqi Security Forces to counter improvised explosive devices, as well as in tactical weapons and combat tactics.

sections.label: SAF savings last year
sections.summary: SAF saved $200 million last year, the highest in the last four years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: SAF saved $200 million last year, the highest in the last four years.

sections.label: Aerostat aerial surveillance savings
sections.summary: The aerostat provides continuous aerial surveillance like a radar plane but saves about $29 million a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Our aerostat achieves continuous aerial surveillance, just like a plane with radar, but saves about $29 million a year.

sections.label: Unmanned towers watch Jurong Island
sections.summary: The Army will build unmanned towers to watch Jurong Island and surrounding waters 24/7, cutting soldiers required by a third.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Instead of soldiers conducting surveillance from observation towers, the Army will build unmanned towers to watch over Jurong Island and the surrounding waters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Those towers will watch 24/7 in all-weather conditions, and it will reduce the total number of soldiers required by a third – a significant number.

sections.label: Unmanned vessels for patrols
sections.summary: Unmanned vessels will soon be used for patrols and underwater surveys.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Unmanned vessels will soon be used for patrols and underwater surveys.

sections.label: CUES practice with ADMM-Plus
sections.summary: All 18 ADMM-Plus countries agreed to adopt CUES and practise it in the 2019 exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We do not even have to wait for the China-ASEAN Maritime Exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We are going to do it with all 18 ADMM-Plus countries – practise CUES, because they have agreed collectively to adopt CUES and practise it in our exercise in 2019.

sections.label: SAF training facilities in Queensland
sections.summary: SAF training facilities will be constructed in Queensland, Australia, due to begin in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For Australia, we will construct SAF training facilities in Queensland, due to begin in 2019.

sections.label: Next-Gen SAF capabilities and Budget
sections.summary: The next-Gen SAF will use new technologies, unmanned systems and advanced weapons, and Members voted for Budget 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The next-Gen SAF will use game-changing technologies and new fighting concepts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: On the ground, they will operate unmanned, autonomous systems, to multiply their forces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Our skies will be better protected with advanced weapons systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We recently added our Aérospatiale Terminale (ASTER)-30, which are here.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: That is what we are investing in, and we will be equipped to deal with ever-evolving cyber threats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: That Members of this House voted for Budget 2018 yesterday, sends a strong signal to our own people and to the world.

sections.label: NS as SAF backbone
sections.summary: NS has been the SAF's backbone since 1967, deterring adversaries and establishing peace for Singapore over 50 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Without a strong SAF, there is no economic future, there is no security.” The Members of this House who voted for the Budget yesterday united themselves with this belief and the resolve of the Pioneer Generation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, since its introduction in 1967, NS had served as the backbone of the SAF and has been instrumental in deterring potential adversaries and establishing the bedrock of peace for Singapore over the last 50 years.

sections.label: SAF manpower reduction by 2030
sections.summary: The Minister for Defence noted last year that SAF will see a one-third reduction in manpower supply by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: As Members of this House will recall, the Minister for Defence noted last year that SAF will see a one-third reduction in manpower supply by 2030.

sections.label: Vocational Interest Initiative for enlistees
sections.summary: The Vocational Interest Initiative considers enlistees' interests when determining the NS vocation they are suitable for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Vocational Interest Initiative allows enlistees’ interests to be taken into consideration when determining the NS vocation that they are suitable to be deployed to.

sections.label: Early findings of Vocational Interest Initiative
sections.summary: Since last November two or three cohorts enlisted, one completed BMT, and MINDEF was asked for early findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Since the launch of the initiative last November, I believe there have been two or three cohorts being enlisted, and one having completed their Basic Military Training (BMT).

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can MINDEF share any early findings of this initiative?

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, according to CSA, there had been a spate of cyberattacks in Singapore over the past year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some of these advanced persistent threats (APTs) had malware signatures that are unknown, even to the anti-malware databases.

sections.label: Cyberattacks on public organisations
sections.summary: Some sophisticated cyberattacks appeared targeted at public organisations to gain access to critical information and data.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Notably, some of these sophisticated cyberattacks appeared to be targeted at public organisations in an effort to gain access to critical information and data.

sections.label: MINDEF Cyber NSF Scheme
sections.summary: MINDEF announced a Cyber NSF Scheme to tap cyber talent in the NSF pool, and was asked for an update.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As part of the ongoing efforts to strengthen its cyber defence capabilities, MINDEF recently announced the launch of a Cyber NSF Scheme to tap on cyber talent with the requisite aptitude and skills of the NSF pool.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide and update on the recently announced Cyber NSF Scheme?

sections.label: ACCORD establishment and restructuring
sections.summary: MINDEF established ACCORD in 1984 for community feedback on defence, and restructured it in 2014 into a main council and three sub-councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: ACCORD was established by MINDEF in 1984 as a channel for the community to provide feedback on issues concerning Singapore’s defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In 2014, it was restructured to comprise the ACCORD main council and three sub-councils covering Employer and Business Council, Family and Community, and Educational Institutions.

sections.label: Full-time NS and economic defence
sections.summary: Full-time NS is the natural starting point for promoting understanding of individual contribution to workforce performance as economic defence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The natural starting point for promoting and understanding how individual contribution to workforce performance is part of economic defence, is full-time NS.

sections.label: Productivity of NSFs
sections.summary: The NS experience offers a chance to inculcate a productivity-driven work ethic in NSFs, and asks what can assess and improve their productivity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Intensity and pervasiveness of the experience present a valuable opportunity for inculcating a productivity-driven work ethic in NSFs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition to ensuring that the skills picked up in NS are relevant to the needs of the economy, what can be done to take advantage of opportunities to assess and improve the individual productivity performance of NSFs?

sections.label: Total Defence and disinformation
sections.summary: Total Defence was launched in 1984 to unite Singaporeans for a resilient nation, and today faces emerging threats such as disinformation campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Chairman, Total Defence was launched in 1984 to galvanise every Singaporean to play our part in building a strong, secure and cohesive nation that is resilient against any crises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Today, we are confronted with emerging threats, such as disinformation campaigns, that can be more insidious because they target the hearts and minds of our people over the long run and are harder to detect.

sections.label: Inter-ethnic marriages and social media
sections.summary: More inter-ethnic and transnational marriages are seen, and the population increasingly relies on social media for news, making them susceptible to misinformation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Over the years, we have seen more inter-ethnic and transnational marriages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Compounding the challenge, our population is also increasingly reliant on social media to get news and information on current affairs, making them more susceptible to misinformation online.

sections.label: ISIS foreign fighters in Southeast Asia
sections.summary: In Southeast Asia, the return of ISIS foreign fighters to their homeland has resulted in a persistent threat of radicalisation in the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Southeast Asia, the return of ISIS foreign fighters to their homeland has resulted in the persistent threat of radicalisation in our region.

sections.label: Singaporeans active social media users
sections.summary: The Business Times reported that 70% of Singaporeans are active social media users on the go, more than double the global average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The Business Times reported that 70% of Singaporeans are active social media users on the go, more than double the global average.

sections.label: State actors using fake news
sections.summary: An even more worrying development is the allegation that state actors may also be involved in using fake news to influence other countries' politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: An even more worrying development is the allegation that state actors may also be involved in using fake news to influence the politics of other countries.

sections.label: MINDEF and fake news threat
sections.summary: A question asks whether MINDEF is concerned about the fake news threat to defence, particularly from state actors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Is MINDEF concerned about this threat of fake news for our defence, particularly where it comes from state actors?

sections.label: NS enrolment and cyber warfare
sections.summary: NS enrolment will decrease by 30% by 2030, and the future of warfare may be in the cyber domain.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: Our NS enrolment will decrease by 30% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: The future of warfare may be in the cyber domain.

sections.label: Engaging families of NSmen
sections.summary: ACCORD has partnered organisations to engage NSmen's families through information sessions and events, and asks how the Ministry can step up such engagement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Thus, families are an important group of people that we can engage to ensure the well-being of our NSmen and NS as an institution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Thus far, ACCORD has partnered the Singapore Council of Women's Organisations (SCWO), the Women's Integration Network of the People's Association and the Young Women's Leadership connection to engage the mothers, wives and girlfriends of our NSmen through information sharing sessions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: ACCORD has also collaborated with the Families for Life Council to engage NSmen and their families, and Families for Life events, such as the Families for Life NS 50 Picnic, held at the Singapore Discovery Centre in August 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Looking ahead, how can the Ministry step up its engagement of families so that they are better able to support our NSmen in their NS journey?

sections.label: Singaporeans performing NS since 1967
sections.summary: Since 1967, more than one million Singaporeans have invested their time and effort in performing their NS duties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Since 1967, more than one million Singaporeans have invested their time and their blood, sweat and tears in faithfully performing their NS duties.

sections.label: Demographic and security threat challenges
sections.summary: The first challenge is demographic, with falling cohort sizes and a shrinking enlistment pool; the second is evolving unconventional security threats such as terrorism, cyberattacks and disinformation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The first challenge, which is a question by Mr Zainal Sapari, is demographic, leading to falling cohort sizes and a shrinking enlistment pool.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The second challenge is the evolving new unconventional security threats, such as terrorism, cyberattacks and also disinformation campaigns or fake news.

sections.label: Full implementation of One BMT
sections.summary: From this year, the One BMT programme will be fully implemented, with combat-fit NSFs enlisting to BMTC on Pulau Tekong for a common nine-week BMT.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From this year, we will fully implement the One BMT programme, where practically all combat-fit NSFs will undergo the Pulau Tekong experience.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, mono-intake units will now be enlisted to BMTC on Pulau Tekong for a common nine-week BMT and stay together as a unit from the start of their NS journey.

sections.label: SAF deploying servicemen to new vocations
sections.summary: Since last year, SAF has deployed more than 600 servicemen to vocations they were previously ineligible for.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Since last year, SAF has deployed more than 600 servicemen to vocations that they were previously ineligible for.

sections.label: Inaugural intake of vocation-interest NSFs
sections.summary: The inaugural intake of about 4,000 NSFs who indicated their vocation interest will be deployed to their respective vocations later this month.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The inaugural intake of about 4,000 NSFs who indicated their vocation interest will be deployed to their respective vocations later this month.

sections.label: Next generation naval base screening
sections.summary: A next generation screening system using biometrics, facial recognition and automated threat analysis will cut security personnel at naval bases by 70% while maintaining or improving security.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It uses a next generation screening system, using technologies, such as biometric authentication, facial recognition and automated threat analysis systems.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: These improvements will reduce the number of security personnel required in the naval bases by 70%, while maintaining the same or an even better level of security.

sections.label: E-fitting kit exchanges reduced
sections.summary: The e-fitting system has reduced kit exchanges at BMTC from 20% to 6%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The e-fitting system has also successfully reduced kit exchanges at BMTC from 20% to 6%.

sections.label: We Support YOU in NS
sections.summary: The "We Support YOU in NS" initiative was launched to rally the community to support NS and recognise servicemen, riding on NS50 momentum.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will continue to ride on the NS50 momentum to rally the community to support NS and recognise our servicemen.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have launched the “We Support YOU in NS” initiative to do so.

sections.label: NS Mark Accreditation Scheme progress
sections.summary: About 2,000 companies and organisations pledged support for NS under the NS Mark Accreditation Scheme launched in 2016, with over 35% attaining NS Mark (Gold).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will continue to encourage employers like them to do so and also encourage employers to have NS-friendly human resource (HR) policies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have made good progress since the launch of the NS Mark Accreditation Scheme in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: About 2,000 companies and organisations came on board to pledge their support for NS.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: More than 35% of these companies have also attained NS Mark (Gold).

sections.label: WSQ-accredited Certificate of Service
sections.summary: The Certificate of Service was enhanced in January to recognise qualities and skills through WSQ accreditation, with about 96% of NSFs going through WSQ-accredited training.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In January this year, we enhanced the Certificate of Service to recognise these qualities, as well as skills, through a statement of attainment for our Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) accreditation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, about 96% of our NSFs will go through NS training that will be WSQ-accredited, especially those in areas, such as Signals, Supply, Logistics, Maintenance, and even Commanders' training as well.

sections.label: Singapore's Total Defence strategy
sections.summary: Singapore's Total Defence strategy encapsulates everyone playing their part to safeguard Singapore, introduced in 1984 against the threat of armed military conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore’s Total Defence strategy encapsulates what everyone playing their part to safeguard Singapore looks like.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: It was introduced in 1984 against the backdrop of the prevailing threat of armed military conflict that can affect many different aspects of our society.

sections.label: MINDEF MHA Mediacorp documentary-drama
sections.summary: MINDEF and MHA worked with Mediacorp on a national security documentary-drama that aired on Channel 5 in January.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To cite a recent example, MINDEF and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) worked with Mediacorp to develop a national security documentary-drama, "It Will Never Happen Here", which aired on Channel 5 in January.

sections.label: MINDEF 2017 Total Defence survey
sections.summary: A 2017 MINDEF public survey showed most respondents appreciated Total Defence's value against conventional and unconventional threats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: A public survey conducted by MINDEF in 2017 showed that a majority of respondents appreciated the value of Total Defence in dealing with threats, both conventional and unconventional.

sections.label: Yu Lun Butterworks video company
sections.summary: Yu Lun set up a video production company and YouTube channel Butterworks, whose films have over 700,000 combined views.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Yu Lun went on to set up his own video production company and YouTube channel "Butterworks" – the people behind films like "The First Book Out from Tekong" and "With Pride, We Lead", that have a combined reach of over 700,000 views.

sections.label: Total Defence new security environment
sections.summary: Total Defence will be geared towards the new security environment, with greater attention to social and psychological defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: As we move forward, just as we are building up the Next-Gen SAF, we will gear Total Defence towards the new security environment, according greater attention to social and psychological defence.

sections.label: ISIS fighter propaganda videos
sections.summary: Two propaganda videos featuring a Singaporean ISIS fighter in Syria surfaced last year, one rallying others and one graphic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Just last year, two propaganda videos featuring a Singaporean ISIS fighter in Syria surfaced – the first video was of him rallying others to join him, while the other video was more graphic, showing him shooting three men at close range.

sections.label: Social cohesion and divisive falsehoods
sections.summary: Social cohesion could be compromised if Singaporeans are swayed by divisive falsehoods or stigmatise groups after a violent attack.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Our social cohesion could be compromised or affected if Singaporeans allow themselves to be swayed by divisive falsehoods, or stigmatise particular social groups in the wake of a violent attack.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Religion today has been misused by terror groups like ISIS and misrepresented by preachers who espouse extreme views.

sections.label: CDC interfaith dialogue programme
sections.summary: The five CDCs launched a nationwide interfaith dialogue programme giving community members a safe space to learn about different faiths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Just last month, the five Community Development Councils (CDCs) launched the "Common Senses for Common Spaces" interfaith dialogue programme nationwide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: This provides members of the community with a safe space to ask questions and learn more about the different faiths in Singapore, thus deepening their understanding and appreciation.

sections.label: Fake news and Psychological Defence
sections.summary: Fake news can undermine Singapore from within and is a key challenge leading MINDEF to focus more on Psychological Defence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Fake news has the potential to undermine us from within and is a key challenge that has led MINDEF to focus more on Psychological Defence.

sections.label: SAFVC volunteers and roles
sections.summary: Since SAFVC launched in 2014, over 600 volunteers were trained and deployed, and in 2018 volunteers can serve in 15 additional roles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: To address Dr Teo Ho Pin's query, since SAFVC was launched in 2014, we have trained over 600 volunteers and deployed them to various roles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: In 2018, volunteers will be able to serve in 15 additional roles across SAF.

sections.label: Community Response Module rollout
sections.summary: A Community Response Module supplements personnel skills, has been rolled out in BMT, and all MINDEF and SAF personnel must undergo it within two years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: In the face of terrorism, we have developed a Community Response Module to supplement the skills that our personnel like Mr Rajendran possess.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: It has been rolled out in the BMT curriculum, and in the next two years, all MINDEF and SAF personnel will be required to go through the module.

sections.label: Guardians of the City card game
sections.summary: The 2017 GOTC card game helps youths understand the terror threat, with over 38,000 decks given to Secondary 2 students this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: The "Guardians of the City" (GOTC) card game launched in 2017 is one way through which we are helping our youths understand the terror threat facing Singapore, and how they can respond.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: This year, we have given out over 38,000 decks of the game to all Secondary 2 students, and schools have organised GOTC cohort experiences.

sections.label: National Education activities and events
sections.summary: National Education activities and milestone events help youths understand security challenges, including heritage visits, the weapon presentation ceremony and a 24-kilometre route march.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: One part of this is National Education activities and milestone events that help them understand what our security challenges are, what we are defending and why and what we must do to continue keeping Singapore safe and secure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: These include experiential visits to defence-related heritage sites, the weapon presentation ceremony and the 24-kilometre route march from Changi to Marina Bay.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: The route march also symbolically reverses the Prisoners-of-War route of defeat from the city to Changi after Singapore fell to our invaders during World War Two.

sections.label: SAF engaging NSmen families
sections.summary: SAF engages NSmen families through events like milestone parades, unit family days and open houses, and gives them information on NS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: SAF has been engaging families of NSmen through events, such as milestone parades, unit family days and open houses, and also provides them with information on NS.

sections.label: SAF deployment to Iraq
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister for Defence about SAF troop deployment to Iraq, its duration, mission, objectives and mission creep concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: My question is directed to the Minister for Defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I understand, Sir, there was an announcement made of the deployment of SAF troops to Iraq.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Thirdly, how long does the Ministry envisage the deployment to last and what is the SAF's mission and objectives with respect to this deployment, and is MINDEF concerned about the prospect of mission creep?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Fourthly, and this is the final question, Singapore deployed about 470 servicemen to Afghanistan from 2007 to 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: They assisted the Afghan National Army Artillery training, improvised explosive device (IED) detection, construction and imagery analysis.

sections.label: Risks of sending personnel
sections.summary: Personnel are sent only when risks are necessary to protect Singaporeans and Singapore, since risks always exist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We must never prepare to send people if you think there are no risks, because there are always risks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We only send them when the risks are necessary to protect Singaporeans and Singapore.

sections.label: Afghanistan terrorism at source
sections.summary: Dealing with terrorism at its source in Afghanistan was understood as necessary, and Singapore was there for 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, for Afghanistan, we understood that if we did not deal with terrorism at its source where Al Qaeda influence was the greatest, you would basically just be responding to waves and waves of terrorists that are being radicalised – they are being trained, they are being exported from ground zero as it were.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We were in Afghanistan for 10 years, Mr Pritam Singh recollected accurately.

sections.label: Needs-and-threats assessment team
sections.summary: For each mission, a needs-and-threats assessment team goes to the ground and produces an assessment of threats and risks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Our SAF personnel who go there recognise that these are threats but we, systemically, identify the threats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, for each mission, we would have a needs-and-threats assessment team that goes down to the ground, that speaks to the commanders, that maps the terrain, that maps the risks and the team will come up with an assessment.

sections.label: Imagery analysts in ISIS mission
sections.summary: Imagery analyst teams were deployed to identify financial strongholds used by ISIS troops and help the coalition eliminate them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Our imagery analyst teams − the Member asked what they were deployed there for – to identify financial strongholds that ISIS troops had been using and help the coalition eliminate these, if you like, financial warehouses.

sections.label: MINDEF Changi Regional Humanitarian Centre
sections.summary: MINDEF engages and works with others through the Changi Regional Humanitarian Centre.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: How is MINDEF engaging and working together with them?

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: That is the kernel of the idea behind the Changi Regional Humanitarian Centre.

sections.label: Expanded centre links with UN
sections.summary: The centre was set up to coordinate military responses and has been expanded to link up with the UN.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, even though our C-130s were sent there, they could not be deployed optimally.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We set up this to coordinate military responses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But as Prof Fatimah Lateef rightly points out, humanitarian agencies include the whole ecosystem of civil groups, of UN groups.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, we have expanded it and linked up with the UN.

sections.label: Weeding out videos, legal action
sections.summary: There is strong reason to identify and weed out such videos by finding the source and potentially taking legal action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: But it could be, if our psychological defence is not strong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: There is actually very strong reason to identify and take steps to weed out such videos either by, first of all, finding out the source; and secondly, potentially, to take legal action against the people who put up and circulate this.
